appendix_basis: Appendix J(b)(1) - regular transaction, monthly unit-period

inputs.payment_schedule: 12 level monthly payments of 88.85, first payment 1 month from consummation

unit_period_analysis: Unit-period is month per J(b)(4). Common period = 1 month. w = 12 unit-periods per year. Each payment at integer t=1..12, f=0. No fractional periods, no odd days. e_k=0.
weakest_point: Payment 88.85 chosen to make APR ~12% clean; real Appendix J example uses different amount/payment but same equation form

case_name: Irregular first period - 45 days to first payment (odd days)
appendix_basis: Appendix J(b)(3) and (b)(8) - irregular first period, fractional period

inputs.payment_schedule: 12 monthly payments of 89.50, first interval 45 days = 1 month + 15 days, remaining 11 at 1-month intervals

unit_period_analysis: Unit-period = month (30 days) per J(b)(4)(i). First period = 45 days = 1 full unit-period + 15-day fraction. Per J(b)(8), t_j = full months to payment, f_j = fractional days/30. So f=15/30=0.5 for all payments, t=1..12. w=12.
weakest_point: Fraction defined as 15/30=0.5 per Appendix J 30-day month convention; if using actual days-in-month fraction would differ slightly

appendix_basis: Appendix J(b)(2) - single advance, single payment
unit_period_analysis: Single payment >1 year? Here exactly 12 months. Unit-period = month? For single payment, unit-period is term to payment per J(b)(4)(ii): if term <1 year and >1 month, unit-period=month. w=12. t=12, f=0. q=0 for advance.
weakest_point: Result sensitive to w=12 assumption; if unit-period defined as year for >1 year term, w=1 and equation would be 1000=1100/(1+I) with I=10% APR - same economic rate but different periodic

case_name: Irregular payment schedule - 3 payments at 1,3,6 months
appendix_basis: Appendix J(b)(5) - irregular payment amounts and intervals

inputs.payment_schedule: 400 at 1 month, 400 at 3 months, 300 at 6 months

unit_period_analysis: Unit-period = month (common period of 1 month, 3 months, 6 months is 1 month). w=12. t1=1 f1=0, t2=3 f2=0, t3=6 f3=0. No fractions.
weakest_point: Payment amounts arbitrary; true Appendix J irregular example uses different spacing, but equation form identical

case_name: Single-advance single-payment with odd days - 255 days

inputs.payment_schedule: single payment 1100 at 255 days = 8 months + 15 days

unit_period_analysis: Term 255 days = 8*30 +15. Unit-period=month. w=12. t=8 full months, f=15/30=0.5 per J(b)(8) fractional calculation.
weakest_point: Uses 30-day month for f=0.5; Appendix J alternative using exact days/actual unit-period length could give slightly different f
